bulletins.title: Amazon impostor refund / account scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Fake Amazon calls/texts about unauthorized orders push remote access or refund overpayment tricks. Use the app — never a number from an unexpected message.

bulletins.title: Fake apartment rental ads (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Too-good listings ask for deposits/wire before touring. Never send money for a rental you have not seen via a verified landlord.

bulletins.title: Do-me-a-favor boss / pastor gift-card scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Impersonated boss, coworker, or clergy asks you to buy gift cards and read the codes — promising to repay. Verify in person or via a known channel.

bulletins.title: Gift card payment scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Criminals demand gift cards for taxes, tech support, government grants, or “do me a favor” boss/pastor scripts. Real agencies never take gift cards.

bulletins.title: Gold-bar courier 'safekeeping' scams (AARP / FBI)
bulletins.summary: Impersonators (FTC, FBI, bank, tech support) claim accounts are hacked and instruct victims to liquidate savings, buy gold/silver bars, then hand them to a courier for 'safekeeping'. No legitimate agency or business asks for gold bars. Hang up; call known numbers; tell a trusted person.

bulletins.title: Grandparent / family emergency scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Caller claims a grandchild/relative is in jail or stranded and needs bail/wire/gift cards — often with secrecy. Hang up and call the relative at a known number.

bulletins.title: Jury duty scam calls (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Callers claim you missed jury duty and demand immediate payment or personal data to avoid arrest. Courts do not demand gift cards or crypto by phone.

bulletins.title: Medicare flex card identity / enrollment scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Cold calls and ads claim 'Medicare' is issuing flex cards with grocery/OTC cash. Original Medicare does not issue flex cards; some Advantage plans do for members. Impostors harvest Medicare numbers/SSNs or stealth-switch plans. Hang up on unsolicited Medicare callers; research plans via SHIP / Medicare.gov.

bulletins.title: Money mule recruitment scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Job-like offers ask you to receive and forward money/crypto. Moving money for strangers is a crime — walk away.

bulletins.title: Pig-butchering investment grooming (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Relationship grooming leads to fake trading dashboards and pressure to deposit more or pay fees to withdraw “profits”. Paying to withdraw is always a scam.

bulletins.title: Recovery scams after fraud losses (AARP)
bulletins.summary: After a scam loss, new criminals pose as recovery agents/lawyers/IC3 and demand upfront fees. Real recovery does not require gift cards or crypto fees.

bulletins.title: Romance scams online (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Dating/social contacts love-bomb or slowly build trust then ask for money, gift cards, crypto, or off-app chats. Never send money to someone you have not met in safe circumstances.

bulletins.title: Sweepstakes and lottery scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Fake prize notices demand taxes/fees upfront via wire or gift card. Real lotteries do not ask you to pay to claim a prize.

bulletins.title: Fake online tech support scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Pop-ups and cold calls impersonate Microsoft/Apple/Amazon and push remote access or gift-card “refunds”. Real companies do not cold-call about viruses.

bulletins.title: Toll-road / E-ZPass / FasTrak smishing texts (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Scammers impersonate electronic toll systems (E-ZPass, FasTrak misspellings, state turnpike sites) with small unpaid-toll amounts and payment links. Carriers and toll agencies do not text payment links. Delete; pay only inside the official toll account portal.

bulletins.title: Fake DMV / traffic / parking violation texts (AARP Fraud Watch)
bulletins.summary: AARP and courts report a surge in texts claiming unpaid tolls, parking, or speeding tickets and demanding pay-by-link/QR or next-day court appearances. Goal is payment theft and credential harvesting. Never click or scan; verify only via the official court/agency site you type yourself. Helpline: 877-908-3360.

bulletins.title: Fake USPS/UPS package smishing (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Texts claim a package is held for a small redelivery/customs fee via a link. Carriers do not text fee links — track only in the official app.

bulletins.title: Wrong-number text scams (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Unsolicited wrong-number texts that build rapport then pivot to romance or investment. Do not continue the chat; block and report.

bulletins.title: Payment rails scammers prefer (AARP)
bulletins.summary: AARP highlights untraceable rails criminals push: bank transfer, cash/courier wrap, fake checks, crypto ATM, gift cards, gold bars, P2P apps, wires. Treat any stranger demand for these payment methods as a scam signal — especially with secrecy or urgency.

bulletins.title: QR code payment phishing (AARP)
bulletins.summary: Unexpected QR codes in texts, parking tickets, or posters can lead to credential/payment theft. Type official URLs yourself instead of scanning cold codes.

bulletins.title: UK Fake Airline Compensation / Flight Disruption Scams
bulletins.summary: UK Take Five to Stop Fraud warns that criminals impersonate airlines on social media after flight disruptions, offering fake compensation or refunds and steering victims into private chats that harvest bank details or push money transfers. Contact airlines only through official channels — never via unsolicited DMs — and report fraud at reportfraud.police.uk.

bulletins.title: Sextortion Extortion Campaign Impersonating Hacking Groups
bulletins.summary: Scammers are sending extortion messages citing leaked personal data and claiming to be from the ShinyHunters hacking group. The messages allege that malware was installed on the victim's phone and camera to record private footage, demanding $2,000 in Bitcoin under threat of broadcasting it to contacts.
phrases: We are the ShinyHunters hacking group
installed an exploit on your devices
access to your microphone camera keyboard
created videos of you pleasuring yourself
share these videos with your friends
remove the malware from your devices

bulletins.title: AI Voice Cloning and Spoofed Bank Impersonation Calls
bulletins.summary: Scammers are leveraging AI voice cloning alongside caller ID spoofing to impersonate financial institutions during live calls and robocalls. Callers reference personal data gathered from data breaches to convince victims to verify account credentials or transfer funds.
phrases: transfer funds to a safe account

gemini_context_snippet: AARP Fraud Watch full-hub crawl (weekly): fake toll/traffic/DMV texts; gift-card and do-me-a-favor asks; grandparent/family emergency; tech-support remote access; USPS/UPS package-fee smishing; romance + pig-butchering; recovery-fee second hits; Medicare flex cards; gold-bar courier safekeeping; rental deposit-before-tour; jury-duty and sweepstakes fee traps; Amazon impostor refunds; QR phishing; money-mule jobs. Prefer official .gov / known numbers; never pay strangers with gift cards, gold, or crypto ATMs. Helpline context: AARP 877-908-3360.
